results.content:

### 14:Overmind

Hello, astronauts!

We have collected all the feedback for demo 14: Overmind and processed it.

We thank all the players who have left feedback about the game. We pay special attention to bug issues, as we want to provide you with a comfortable and interesting space adventure.

In this post, we will answer the most popular complaints about the game.

CRASHES   
Unfortunately, we cannot fully understand Crash's mistake. Crashes occur for some players, but we cannot reproduce the specific circumstances under which errors occur.  If you encounter a similar problem, please email us.

Tell us in detail about the error that occurred, if possible, attach a screenshot or screen recording, and also write the configuration data of your PC. [...] PERFORMANCE ERRORS    
According to reports, some players were experiencing performance issues. The most popular mistake is the lack of components that meet the minimum system requirements of the game. Please note: 14: Overmind does not support 10th series graphics cards!    
   
  
BUGS  
Thanks to the Games of Being, we have received a large number of bug reports and have already begun to solve them. We apologize to those for whom bugs have become a serious obstacle to enjoying our game.

THE "TORSION" ERROR   
The "twist" is triggered when the gamepad is connected. Demo version 14: Overmind DOES NOT SUPPORT controllers. If the error is reproduced without the gamepad, please email us. [...] Tell us in detail about the error that occurred, if possible, attach a screenshot or screen recording, and also write the configuration data of your PC.

LOCALIZATION ERRORS   
As the reviews have shown, there are grammatical and spelling errors in the demo. Although there are few of them, one way or another we have to pay attention to them. A separate discussion has been created in the community center where you can report a linguistic error. 

If you encounter any errors, write about them in the Community Center.

Thanks again to everyone who played the game and left a review. Thanks to you, we will be able to make an amazing space!

Astronauts!

The "Next Fest" is over!

results.title: The Overmind Story
results.content:
After some testing and approvals we rolled out the change and everything was looking good, there weren’t any errors being reported and we could now log in to servers with our regular user accounts which was perfect. Only 45 minutes until the pub.

##### ‍The PDF Printer Fiasco

Then the phone started to ring…

> Hey I can’t save PDFs anymore!”

Wait, what? I think to myself. We haven’t touched any laptops, how could we possibly have broken the ability to save PDFs? Turns out a whole department was basically at a standstill because nobody could save PDFs and this was absolutely critical to their workflow. [...] We started frantically looking into it and it turns out that they aren’t clicking Print -> Save as PDF like you’d expect, they have an actual printer called “PDF Printer” that they print to instead, which it appears we've broken somehow.

##### ‍Unearthing the Hidden Server

We asked around, but nobody knew about it. There was a wiki, but it wasn't mentioned. There was a CMDB, but it wasn't in there. We ended up just discovering the IP address of this "printer" and trying to log in via SSH, which worked! What followed then was a particularly complicated session of infrastructure palaeontology which, much like regular palaeontology, is much more tedious and less interesting than Indiana Jones makes it look, but we eventually cracked it! # The Overmind Story

The Overmind Story

‍‍A few years ago when I was consulting in London, we’d just finished implementing some automation and were planning to roll out a big change on a Friday afternoon to show it off.

Firstly, this is a bad idea, as Captain Jim Hopper would say "[Fridays] are for coffee and contemplation", not rolling out big changes, plus we had a pub to be at in just over 2 hours…

##### An Unexpected Twist with User Logins

‍The change we were making was related to the way the backend UNIX fleet authenticated user logins so should have been fairly innocuous, but could definitely still go wrong.
